react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms—RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA—converge on tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelmingly dominant perturbed pathway. Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380, WP:WP465) achieves Rank #0 in all three tools simultaneously, with FDR scores ranging from 5.6×10⁻¹⁸ (RaMP) to p=9.2×10⁻⁴ (Mummichog) and p=1.6×10⁻⁸ (MetaboAnalystR), representing a rare triple-paradigm consensus at the top rank. Seven of the ten input metabolites map directly to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. The pathway's two major branches are both represented—serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931, FDR=3.4×10⁻⁸) and the kynurenine/NAD⁺ branch (WP4210, WP3645, WP2485, all FDR <10⁻⁷). The IDO metabolic pathway (WP5414) is the single most enriched entity by fold-enrichment (1637×), consistent with immunometabolic reprogramming under inflammatory or treatment conditions. Arginine and proline metabolism (MUMM:arginine_and_proline_metabolism, p=0.026) emerges as a secondary signal via Mummichog, driven by 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid. L-valine contributes to a weak Valine, leucine and isoleucine biosynthesis signal (KEGG:hsa00290, p=0.044) that does not replicate across paradigms. The biological story is one of broad tryptophan catabolism reprogramming: the treatment condition simultaneously alters the serotonin-melatonin neuroendocrine axis and the kynurenine-NAD⁺ immunometabolic axis, consistent with inflammatory cytokine-driven IDO activation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis paradigms—RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA—converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380) as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP ORA ranks this KEGG entry first (FDR 5.56e-18, fold-enrichment 778×, 7 of 54 pathway metabolites hit). Mummichog network-activity analysis returns Tryptophan metabolism at rank 1 (p = 0.0024, 17 of 18 pathway metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranks KEGG:hsa00380 first (p = 1.59e-08, 6 of 41 metabolites hit). Within this dominant hit, L-tryptophan is the entry-point substrate shared across the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 1.36e-08, fold-enrichment 1637×) and the serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.38e-08, fold-enrichment 1200×). 3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid extend the signal into the kynurenine/NAD+ branch, hitting Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.46e-10, fold-enrichment 1044×). L-Valine is also enriched through its membership in Arginine and Proline Metabolism (MUMM:arginine_and_proline_metabolism, p = 0.031), where it is catabolized to 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912), and through Valine, leucine and isoleucine biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00290, p = 0.044) as a primary input metabolite. The tryptophan and proline families together account for 9 of the 10 input metabolites across the two enrichment paradigms.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on Tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) first with FDR = 5.56e-18, hitting 7 of the 10 input metabolites (L-tryptophan, melatonin, quinolinic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, serotonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine); fold-enrichment is 778×. Mummichog m/z-direct activity also ranks Tryptophan metabolism first (p = 0.0024), with all 17 matched compounds falling in that module. The RaMP Reactome entry REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) is also significant at rank 9 (FDR = 3.38e-08, fold-enrichment 1201×), confirming that the serotonin–melatonin arm of tryptophan catabolism is specifically affected. A secondary signal appears in Arginine and Proline Metabolism (MUMM rank 2, p = 0.031), where 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid drive the hit. The driver metabolites L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), melatonin (KEGG:C01598), and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) are verified members of KEGG:map00380 via the RaMP metabolite-hit rosters. Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR = 1.46e-10, fold-enrichment 1044×) is the third-ranked pathway, indicating that the kynurenine branch is also perturbed alongside the neurotransmitter arm.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms—RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA—converge on tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelmingly dominant perturbed pathway. Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380, WP:WP465) achieves Rank #0 in all three tools simultaneously, with FDR scores ranging from 5.6×10⁻¹⁸ (RaMP) to p=9.2×10⁻⁴ (Mummichog) and p=1.6×10⁻⁸ (MetaboAnalystR), representing a rare triple-paradigm consensus at the top rank. Seven of the ten input metabolites map directly to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. The pathway's two major branches are both represented—serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931, FDR=3.4×10⁻⁸) and the kynurenine/NAD⁺ branch (WP4210, WP3645, WP2485, all FDR <10⁻⁷). The IDO metabolic pathway (WP5414) is the single most enriched entity by fold-enrichment (1637×), consistent with immunometabolic reprogramming under inflammatory or treatment conditions. Arginine and proline metabolism (MUMM:arginine_and_proline_metabolism, p=0.026) emerges as a secondary signal via Mummichog, driven by 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid. L-valine contributes to a weak Valine, leucine and isoleucine biosynthesis signal (KEGG:hsa00290, p=0.044) that does not replicate across paradigms. The biological story is one of broad tryptophan catabolism reprogramming: the treatment condition simultaneously alters the serotonin-melatonin neuroendocrine axis and the kynurenine-NAD⁺ immunometabolic axis, consistent with inflammatory cytokine-driven IDO activation.
